newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Jan palm oil output seen down 9.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Jan palm oil output seen down 9.5 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in January is estimated to have fallen by 9.5 percent to 578,000 tonnes from December 1996, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Wednesday.
Wong put palm oil stocks at the end of January at 725,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 792,687 tonnes at end-December.
Exports in January are estimated at 545,000 tonnes against PORLA's 637,899 tonnes in December.
Wong said in a report that the decline in production was marginally more than his previous projection.

"An early cessation of monsoon rains in East Malaysia during the month helped minimised interruptions in harvesting operations and ensured the overall drop in crude palm oil production in Sabah was modest," he said. "Some producers in Sabah even managed to chalk up slight increases in production."
Wong said stocks of crude palm oil are likely to fall further to less than 300,000 tonnes in February from an estimated 375,000 tonnes in January.
Malaysia palm oil supply-demand estimate/projection as of February 5, 1997. (All figures in '000 tonnes)
